Write a polynomial-time reduction from Clique to Vertex Cover. problems.py defines both problems: SOURCE is Clique and TARGET is Vertex Cover. The SOURCE and TARGET class docstrings give the exact instance formats, yes-conditions and edge cases.

PROBLEM DEFINITIONS (the SOURCE and TARGET docstrings from problems.py, complete as given here):

SOURCE = Clique
Clique.

Instance: {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...], "k": k}
  * Vertices are 0..n-1. Edges are undirected pairs [u, v] with u != v;
    [u, v] and [v, u] are the same edge and may not both appear.
  * k is any integer.

Yes iff the graph has a clique of AT LEAST k vertices: k vertices with an
edge between every two of them.

Edge cases: k <= 0 is always yes. k = 1 is yes whenever n >= 1. k > n is
always no.

TARGET = VertexCover
Vertex Cover.

Instance: {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...], "k": k}
  * Vertices are 0..n-1. Edges are undirected pairs [u, v] with u != v;
    [u, v] and [v, u] are the same edge and may not both appear.
  * k is any integer.

Yes iff the graph has a vertex cover of AT MOST k vertices: a set of
vertices that includes at least one endpoint of every edge.

Edge cases: k < 0 is always no. A graph with no edges is yes for every
k >= 0 (the empty set covers it). k >= n is yes, since all vertices cover
every edge.

    """An instance that does not follow its problem's format."""


def require(condition: bool, message: str) -> None:
    if not condition:
        raise InvalidInstance(message)

    return isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool)


def require_keys(instance: Any, keys: set[str]) -> None:
    require(isinstance(instance, dict), "instance must be a dict")
    require(
        set(instance) == keys,
        f"instance keys must be exactly {sorted(keys)}, got {sorted(instance)}",
    )


def require_int(value: Any, field: str, minimum: int | None = None) -> None:
    require(is_int(value), f"{field} must be an int")
    if minimum is not None:
        require(value >= minimum, f"{field} must be >= {minimum}")


def validate_graph(instance: Instance) -> None:
    """Check the "n" and "edges" fields of a graph instance."""
    n = instance.get("n")
    require_int(n, "n", minimum=0)
    edges = instance.get("edges")
    require(isinstance(edges, list), "edges must be a list")
    seen: set[frozenset[int]] = set()
    for edge in edges:
        require(
            isinstance(edge, list) and len(edge) == 2,
            f"each edge must be a list [u, v], got {edge!r}",
        )
        u, v = edge
        require(is_int(u) and is_int(v), f"edge endpoints must be ints, got {edge!r}")
        require(0 <= u < n and 0 <= v < n, f"edge {edge!r} has a vertex outside 0..{n - 1}")
        require(u != v, f"self-loop {edge!r} is not allowed")
        key = frozenset((u, v))
        require(key not in seen, f"duplicate edge {edge!r}")

    require(isinstance(clauses, list), "clauses must be a list")

        for literal in clause:
            require(is_int(literal), f"literals must be ints, got {literal!r}")
            require(
                literal != 0 and abs(literal) <= num_vars,
                f"literal {literal} is outside ±1..±{num_vars}",
            )

    assert isinstance(instance, dict)
    validate_graph(instance)
    require_int(instance["k"], "k")

            f"clause {clause!r} must use 3 different variables",

                all(literal > 0 for literal in clause),
                f"clause {clause!r} must contain only positive literals",
            )

# Validation helpers from benchmark/problems/sets_common.py


def validate_set_system(instance: object, keys: set[str]) -> None:
    require_keys(instance, keys)
    assert isinstance(instance, dict)
    universe_size = instance["universe_size"]
    require_int(universe_size, "universe_size", minimum=0)
    sets = instance["sets"]
    require(isinstance(sets, list), "sets must be a list")
    for subset in sets:
        require(isinstance(subset, list), f"each set must be a list, got {subset!r}")
        for element in subset:
            require(is_int(element), f"elements must be ints, got {element!r}")

    require(isinstance(numbers, list), "numbers must be a list")
    assert isinstance(numbers, list)
    for number in numbers:
        require(is_int(number), f"numbers must be ints, got {number!r}")
        require(number >= 0, f"numbers must be >= 0, got {number}")

# The two problems


class Clique:
    """Clique.

    Instance: {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...], "k": k}
      * Vertices are 0..n-1. Edges are undirected pairs [u, v] with u != v;
        [u, v] and [v, u] are the same edge and may not both appear.
      * k is any integer.

    Yes iff the graph has a clique of AT LEAST k vertices: k vertices with an
    edge between every two of them.

    Edge cases: k <= 0 is always yes. k = 1 is yes whenever n >= 1. k > n is
    always no.
    """

    name = 'Clique'

    @classmethod
    def validate(cls, instance: object) -> None:
        validate_graph_with_k(instance)

    """Vertex Cover.

      * Vertices are 0..n-1. Edges are undirected pairs [u, v] with u != v;

      * k is any integer.

    Yes iff the graph has a vertex cover of AT MOST k vertices: a set of
    vertices that includes at least one endpoint of every edge.

    Edge cases: k < 0 is always no. A graph with no edges is yes for every
    k >= 0 (the empty set covers it). k >= n is yes, since all vertices cover
    every edge.
"

{"command":"apply_patch <<'PATCH'
*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: reduce.py
+"""Reduction from Clique to Vertex Cover.
+
+The reduction uses the classic complement‑graph construction:
+
+* A set of vertices forms a clique in a graph G iff its complement (the set
+  of all other vertices) is a vertex cover in the complement graph \bar{G}.
+* Therefore, an instance ``(G, k)`` of Clique can be transformed into the
+  instance ``(\bar{G}, n - k)`` of VertexCover, where ``n`` is the number of
+  vertices of G.
+
+The function ``reduce`` validates the input using ``Clique.validate`` and then
+produces a dictionary that conforms to the ``VertexCover`` format.  All edge
